List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the August 21, 2007/Sravana 30, 1929 (Saka)

(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture; Finance;

Total number of questions — 20
39
Deficiencies in management of big
PSUs
*121. SHRI SANJAY RAUT:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether CAG has pointed out that
money spent by Government amounting
to Rs. 26,000 crores has not been accounted
for pointing to mammoth sloth and lack of
transparency in the functioning of PSUs
and Central Ministries;
(b) whether some black holes have been
listed by CAG which include failure to
classify accounts;
(c) what are the deficiencies in
management of several big PSUs like FCI,
Airports Authority of India, SAIL, Indian
Oil and ONGC found in the CAG reports;
and
(d) whether while scanning transaction
of major PSUs, CAG has found huge
irregularities with a combined financial
implication estimated to be over Rs. 4500
crore?
Income Tax refund through SBI
*122. SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) the authority which will credit the
taxpayers accounts within three days of an
assessment orders being sent to it in the
recently introduced scheme of Income-Tax
refund through SBI;
(b) how Government would avoid
inordinate delay in assessment process by
Income Tax officials;
(c) whether any study has been made
of the average time taken between the
receipt of the IT return and completion of
its assessment separately, individual,
Corporate Tax-payers-wise; and
(d) if so, what are the findings thereof?

40
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Procurement of gas from Myanmar
†*123. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian
Public Sector Undertakings Gas Authority
of India Ltd. And ONGC Videsh have
10 per cent and 20 per cent stake
respectively in the gas reserves of Block
A1 and A3 situated in Myanmar;
(b) if not, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Myanmar had proposed to sell the gas
produced from the reserves to India;
(d) if so, the time when this proposal
was made and the contents of the proposal;
and
(e) the reasons for not accepting this
proposal?
Promotion of tourism schemes abroad
*124. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
promote schemes like Medical Tourism,
Beach Tourism, Heritage Tourism,
Pilgrimage Tourism and Desert Tourism
abroad before the commencement of
Commonwealth Games in 2010;
(b) if so, the details of Government's
plan; and
(c) the total amount earmarked for
promotion of tourism activity before the
Games?
Erosion control in the North East
*125. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of funds allocated for
erosion control in the North East by the
Brahmaputra River;
(b) the time limit of implementation of
the said projects considering the enormous
loss of land;
(c) whether Government are aware of
the fact that such massive erosion was
taking place;
(d) whether the reasons for the massive
erosion is deforestation; and
(e) if so, whether any dedicated
afforestation projects have been initiated?
Projected requirement in the Luxury
Hospitality Sector
*126. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
in the luxury sector, the projected
requirement for over a period of five years
till 2011, will be around 53,000 rooms across
ten cities;
(b) if so, whether the requirement would
be about 1.38 lakh jobs between
2007-2011, and out of this 94,000 would
be fresh talent; and
(c) whether catering institutes are
capable of producing about one lakh trained
personnel especially when only 20 per cent
of the hotel management graduates opt for
hospitality industry and balance attracted
towards BPOs, Airlines, Call Centres, etc.?

41
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Foreign exchange on Capital Account
*127. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) what are the details of inflow of
foreign exchange on the capital account
during 2006-07, in each category, and which
of these inflows are productive and which
are speculative; and
(b) what corrective action, if any, has
been taken or planned to curb speculative
inflows?
Modernization of non-metro airports

propose to modernize thirty-five non-

(c) what is the budget earmarked by

208
Direct flight from far East countries
to Delhi and Gaya
899. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that tourists and
pilgrims from the far East countries and
specially China are interested in visiting
India, but there are hardly any air
connections;
(b) if so, whether there is any plan to
connect Beijing, Shanghai, Taipeh and
Tokyo directly to Delhi and to Gaya to
facilitate the tourists and pilgrims; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Vision-2020
900. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI:
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) what are the salient features of the
Vision-2020 document prepared by his
Ministry for aviation sector;
(b) whether it is a fact that consolidation
of Indian aviation sector is taking place very
rapidly;
(c) whether the document has been
approved by Cabinet; and
(d) if so, what would be its impact on
the fares and passenger traffic?
Entry of Pawan Hans in regional
airline market
901. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
PSU Pawan Hans is exploring plans to
enter regional airline market with a fleet of
small fixed wing aircrafts that can seat about
20 passengers;
(b) if so, whether Government would
ensure that up-coming districts in  tribal
belt of Vidarbha, like Yavatmal, are given
first preference for introducing such a
service; and
(c) whether  subsidy is also given to
Pawan Hans if they find that the route is
not initially viable as is being done in North
East districts?

209
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Overseas operations by domestic
airlines
902. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated its much-awaited 'Civil Aviation
Policy' with a view to ease the norms for
launching overseas operations by domestic
airlines;
(b) if so, the details thereof indicating,
whether the Airports Authority of India is
likely to be restructured; and
(c) whether the new Policy would also
contain a 'Vision 2020' document that would
lay down a road map for aviation in the
light of recent boom in this sector in country
including giving of final shape to a policy
to promote 'merchant green-field airports'?
Upgradation of airstrips
†903. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a)  the names of different air strips
proposed to be upgraded;
(b) the details of expenditure to be
incurred for this purpose;
(c) whether his Ministry has received
any suggestion regarding construction of
some air-strips by State Government; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Merchant Greenfield Airports
904. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has convened
a meeting of industry representatives as
precursor to giving final shape to a policy
to promote 'Merchant Greenfield Airports'
as the Merchant Greenfield Airports will
be private airports built on private lands
within permissible civil aviation parameters
and air-traffic management regime;
(b) if so, what was the outcome of the
meeting held; and
(c) whether the Ministry has also
stressed the need to 'revisit' the policy on
airports as almost every airport expansion
project is facing problems over land
acquisition?
Profit/loss incurred by airports
†905. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of airports being used
for commercial purpose under Airports
Authority of India;
(b) the number and details of airports
earning profit and those running into loss;
(c) whether the Authority has decided
not to further develop the airports running
into loss; and
(d) if so, whether Birsa Munda Airport
at Ranchi, Jharkhand has been included
among such airports?
Acquisition of modern aircrafts by
Indian
906. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's new airline
company formed with the merger of Air
India and Indian has embarked upon a
massive long term programme for acquiring
modern aircrafts for its use; and

the nature of aircrafts proposed to be
acquired, total funds required for the
purpose, its source and the time-frame for
the completion of the plan?
